findings.evidence: Rose stem projections are prickles, superficial outgrowths, rather than true thorns (modified branches) or spines (modified leaves).
Institutional summaries describe herbivore deterrence and possible water interactions; a peer-reviewed biomechanics study supports an attachment role in leaning/climbing rose stems.
Prickle shape, angle, mechanical behaviour and abundance vary among rose types and cultivated varieties.
A 2024 report from INRAE describes LOG-gene involvement in prickle development across plant groups including roses; that does not by itself prove a single evolutionary purpose.

editorial_angles: Use precise anatomy while acknowledging common everyday terminology.
Defence is an important benefit, not a universal single-cause explanation.
Describe the independently studied mechanical attachment function in leaning rose stems.
Separate developmental gene findings from ecological explanations of function.
Explain differences across species and cultivars without a one-size-fits-all rule.
